content: The Alexander technique is a structured therapeutic approach that involves a series of specific movements aimed at correcting posture and aligning the body in a natural way. This method is intended to enhance the body's functional efficiency and is also reported to promote relaxation. Some practitioners assert that the Alexander technique can provide benefits for individuals seeking improved ease and efficiency in breathing, including those with asthma. The purpose of this review was to assess the effectiveness of the Alexander technique in individuals with chronic, stable asthma. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted using the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register, the Cochrane Complementary Medicine Field trials register, and the bibliographies of relevant articles. The most recent search was completed in June 2012. The review focused on identifying randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that evaluated the use of the Alexander technique for improving symptoms of chronic, stable asthma. These trials were required to compare the Alexander technique either to another intervention or to no intervention at all. However, no studies meeting the specified selection criteria were identified during the search process. Consequently, no meta-analysis could be performed due to the absence of eligible trials. The authors concluded that there is a need for rigorous, well-designed randomized controlled trials to investigate the claims made by practitioners regarding the potential benefits of the Alexander technique for alleviating symptoms of chronic asthma. Such studies are necessary to determine whether this technique can help individuals with asthma reduce their reliance on medication.
